nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Sq-MOFs
nodes.procedure: For the pristine monometallic MOF synthesis, a mixture of 3,4-dihydroxy-3-cyclobutene-1,2-dione (squaric acid) (7.29 mmol, 1.5 eq.), metal (II) chloride hydrate (4.86 mmol, 1 eq.) (M = Co^{2+}, Fe^{2+} or Ni^{2+}), potassium hydroxide (19.4 mmol, 4 eq.), and water (17.5 mL) was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined reactor. After 30 min of sonication, the Teflon-lined reactor was transferred to a preheated oven and heated to 220°C for 72 h. After the reaction, the reactor was slowly cooled and Sq-MOF crystals were isolated using decantation and centrifugation. The Sq-MOF was repeatedly washed with D. I. water, exchanged with acetone and dried. Activation at 120°C for 12 h was performed before gas adsorption measurements. For synthesizing bimetallic Sq-MOFs, the following ratios of mix metal ions were used M1:M2 = 1:3 (M1 = 1.215 mmol, M2 = 3.645 mmol), M1:M2 = 1:2 (M1 = 1.62 mmol, M2 = 3.24 mmol), M1:M2 = 1:1 (M1 = 2.43 mmol, M2 = 2.43 mmol), M1:M2 = 2:1 (M1 = 3.24 mmol, M2 = 1.62 mmol), and M1:M2 = 3:1 (M1 = 3.645 mmol, M2 = 1.215 mmol).

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Monometallic and Bimetallic Squarate MOFs: Sq-MOFs based on metal (II) ... M1:M2 = 3:1 (M1 = 3.645 mmol, M2 = 1.215 mmol).

Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF shows a low overpotential of 230 mV (at 10 mA cm⁻²), a small Tafel slope of 37.7 mV dec⁻¹... LSV analysis demonstrated that Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF could achieve an overpotential of 243 and 260 mV at a current density of 20 and 50 mA cm⁻²... chronoamperometric studies at an overpotential of 255 mV... after 15 h... ≈92% of the OER activity was retained.

At a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², Ni₃Fe₁ and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOFs demonstrated low overpotential values of 250 and 230 mV, respectively... Ni₃Fe₁ and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOFs show a low Tafel slope of 42.8 and 37.7 mV dec⁻¹ respectively.

Co₁Ni₃ Sq-zbr-MOF... shows a lower overpotential of 307 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope analysis... 49.2 mV dec⁻¹... prolonged chronoamperometric test at a constant overpotential of 340 mV... After 15 h... ≈90% of current density was retained.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD confirms zbr topology for Co-Ni, Ni-Fe (up to 33% Fe), and Co-Fe (up to 33% Fe) bimetallic Sq-MOFs; mixed zbr/nbo-b at 1:1 Ni:Fe; pure nbo-b at >50% Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PXRD analysis evidenced that the Co-Ni bimetallic squarate MOFs form the desired zbr topology in all Co²⁺ and Ni²⁺ concentration variations (Figure 2a). However, the nature of these phases in Co-Fe and Ni-Fe bimetallic Sq-MOFs depends on the ratio of the concentration of bimetallic metal ions (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: SXRD analysis confirms Ni Sq-zbr-MOF ([Ni₃(C₄O₄)₂(OH)₂]·2.68H₂O) and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF ([Fe₁Ni₂(C₄O₄)₂(OH)₂]·2.71H₂O) crystallize in monoclinic C2/m space group.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SXRD analysis of Ni Sq-zbr-MOF ([Ni₃(C₄O₄)₂(OH)₂]·2.68H₂O) and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF ([Fe₁Ni₂(C₄O₄)₂(OH)₂] 2.71H2O) revealed that these Sq-zbr-MOFs crystallize in a monoclinic system with a space group C2/m.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows metal squarate linkages with shifted carbonyl stretching bands to 1537 cm⁻¹ and μ³-bridged hydroxyl at ≈3600 cm⁻¹ in Sq-zbr-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) studies demonstrated the formation of metal squarate linkages in a bimetallic squarate system (Figures S2-S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping confirms bimetallic ion ratios in Sq-MOFs proportional to starting metal precursor molar ratios.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping was used to determine the ratio of bimetallic ions in these Sq-MOFs (Figures S5-S8, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA shows bimetallic Co₁Ni₂ and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOFs retain thermal stability up to 300°C after initial 8-10 wt% water loss, similar to monometallic Sq-zbr-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TGA analysis revealed that the thermal stability of bimetallic Co₁Ni₂ and Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOFs was almost similar to that of the pristine monometallic Sq-zbr-MOF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water vapor adsorption at 25°C shows type I reversible uptake ≈10 wt% for Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF, Co Sq-zbr-MOF, and Ni Sq-zbr-MOF, indicating high water affinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To examine the permanent porosity of Sq-MOFs, water vapor adsorption experiments were performed at 25°C. Monometallic Sq-MOFs (Co Sq-zbr-MOF, Ni Sq-zbr-MOF) and bimetallic Sq-MOF (Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF) demonstrate type I reversible water vapor uptake.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD patterns remain unchanged after 3 days treatment in 1.0 M KOH, confirming high chemical stability of monometallic and bimetallic Sq-zbr-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Monometallic and bimetallic Sq-MOFs demonstrate high chemical stability in basic conditions (1.0 M KOH) as revealed by their PXRD patterns, which remained unchanged after this long-term treatment (Figure S11, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER PXRD confirms Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF, Ni₃Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF, Ni Sq-zbr-MOF, and Co₁Ni₃ Sq-zbr-MOF retain crystallinity and characteristic Bragg peaks after long-term testing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PXRD analysis shows that Ni₂Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF and Ni₃Fe₁ Sq-zbr-MOF retain their crystallinity and structural integrity after long-term continuous oxygen evolution test (Figures S14-S16, Supporting Information).
